questions.stem: An antibiotic works by preventing ribosomes from functioning in bacterial cells. Why might this antibiotic not harm human cells?

options.text: Human cells do not have ribosomes
Bacterial ribosomes are structurally different from human ribosomes
Human cells are protected by a cell wall
Human cells do not make proteins

questions.explanation: Bacterial ribosomes (70S) are smaller and structurally different from human ribosomes (80S). Antibiotics can be designed to target only bacterial ribosomes, leaving human ribosomes unaffected. Both cell types do have ribosomes and make proteins.

questions.stem: A bacterial cell is found to be resistant to an antibiotic. The resistance gene is carried on a small circular piece of DNA separate from the main chromosome. What is this structure called?

options.text: Nucleus
Flagellum
Plasmid
Capsule

questions.explanation: Plasmids are small, circular rings of DNA found in bacterial cells that are separate from the main chromosomal DNA. They often carry genes for antibiotic resistance and can be transferred between bacteria, which is why antibiotic resistance can spread rapidly.

questions.stem: A student observes a cell under a microscope. It has no visible nucleus but does have a cell wall. Which additional feature would confirm it is a bacterium rather than a red blood cell?

options.text: The presence of a cell membrane
The cell being very small (1-5 micrometres)
The presence of mitochondria
The cell having chromosomes in a nucleus

questions.explanation: Bacterial cells are typically 1-5 micrometres in size, much smaller than most eukaryotic cells. Red blood cells lack a nucleus but also lack a cell wall. The very small size combined with a cell wall and no nucleus is characteristic of bacteria. Bacteria do not have mitochondria.

questions.stem: Scientists use genetic engineering to insert a human gene into a bacterial plasmid. The bacteria then produce human insulin. Why are bacteria useful for this purpose?

options.text: Bacteria have a nucleus that can store extra genes
Bacteria reproduce very rapidly, producing large quantities of the protein quickly
Bacteria are eukaryotic organisms
Bacteria cannot mutate

questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission very rapidly (as fast as every 20 minutes). This means a single modified bacterium can produce millions of copies of itself, each producing insulin, making large-scale production efficient and cost-effective.

questions.stem: A bacterium has a flagellum and a slime capsule. In which environment would these features give the greatest survival advantage?

options.text: Growing on a sterile agar plate in a lab
Inside the human immune system where white blood cells attack invaders
In a very cold environment
On the surface of dry skin

questions.explanation: The flagellum allows the bacterium to move towards nutrients or away from threats, while the slime capsule protects against the immune system by making it harder for white blood cells to engulf (phagocytose) the bacterium. These features are most advantageous when evading immune responses.
